title: Diameter of Binary Tree
statement: You get the root of a binary tree. Return the length of the longest path between any two nodes, counted in edges. The path may or may not pass through the root. An empty tree and a single node both give 0.

example.caption: The longest path is 4 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3. It uses 3 edges.

idea.sentence: Compute each node's height, and while you are there, check the longest path that bends at that node (left height plus right height).

jargon.plain: The number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes in the tree.
How many nodes are on the longest path from a node down to a leaf. A lone leaf is 1.
One link between a parent and a child.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the tree as a level-order array, null for a missing child, e.g. [1,2,3,4,5]

compare.bruteLabel: Recompute both heights from scratch at every node
compare.optimalLabel: One pass: height and best path together
compare.unit: node visits, for a skinny tree

rows.name: Heights recomputed per node
rows.note: Every node walks down its whole subtree again to measure it.

rows.name: Height and answer in one pass
rows.note: Each node is visited once. The heights it needs were just returned by its children.

fast.takeaway: The height you must return to the parent is the same number you need for the path check, so one walk does both jobs.

stages.title: Start best at 0
stages.note: best remembers the longest path seen so far. It lives outside the recursion.

stages.title: Heights below
stages.note: Recurse left and right. Each call returns the height of its subtree.

stages.title: Check the bend
stages.note: A path that turns at this node uses both sides: left height + right height edges. Keep it if it beats best.

stages.title: Report up
stages.note: Return 1 + the taller side as this node's height. When the recursion ends, best is the answer.

edges.title: Empty tree
edges.why: No nodes, no path. best never moves from 0.

edges.title: Single node
edges.why: A path from a node to itself has no edges.

edges.title: Skips the root
edges.why: The longest path bends at node 2, below the root. Checking only the root's two heights gives 3.

edges.title: Chain
edges.why: One side is empty everywhere, so the path is the whole chain: edges, not nodes.

gotchas.text: The answer is not the root's left height plus right height. The best bend can be at any node. Update best at every node.
Count edges, not nodes. With heights counted in nodes, left + right already equals the edge count of the bend.
Two different numbers leave each call: the height you return, and the path length you save into best. Do not return the path length.
best is captured by the inner arrow function, which is fine. If you passed it as a number parameter instead, the update would be lost on return.
A closure that calls itself must be declared first: var height func(*TreeNode) int, then assigned. height := func... cannot refer to itself.

recap.key: Return the height, and update a running best with left height + right height at every node.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(h) call stack.
moves: left, right = heights of the two children
best = max(best, left + right). Return 1 + max(left, right)
